description: Universe Breakers is a one-person team from Chattogram, Bangladesh. We love space, storytelling and building things for the web. For Space Apps 2026 we built "Solar System Graveyard... or Hall of Fame?", a website where 36 retired NASA machines tell their own stories in the first person, with an AI-narrated voice. Our skills: React, TypeScript, 3D web, writing and design. We are always happy to meet space-minded students and learn from other teams.
summary:
Solar System Graveyard... or Hall of Fame? is an interactive website where NASA's retired machines tell their own stories. Since the 1960s, NASA has left hardware on the Moon, on Mars and in deep space. Some went silent decades ago, some are still travelling, and most students only meet them as lists of dates. We ask one question: are they a graveyard, or a hall of fame?

Each of our 36 machines, from Surveyor 1 to Perseverance and the James Webb Space Telescope, has its own page. It tells its story in the first person, in four short chapters of simple English, with a status badge (still active or gone silent), a Did You Know fact, NASA photos, a quick quiz and a "Listen to my story" audio narration (AI-generated voice). The home page has an interactive 3D solar system. The site is free, needs no account, and installs like an app.

It answers the challenge "Abandoned but not Forgotten" by giving discarded equipment a voice, so a story keeps it from being forgotten. Built by one person, team Universe Breakers, for high school students.
details:
HOW WE ADDRESSED THE CHALLENGE

NASA has left hardware on the Moon, on Mars and in deep space. Some of it went silent decades ago, some is still travelling, and most students only meet these machines as lists of dates. Our answer to "Abandoned but not Forgotten" is simple: give each machine a voice. On our website, 36 retired NASA spacecraft and rovers tell their own stories in the first person, so a story keeps them from being forgotten. We ask one question: are they a graveyard, or a hall of fame?

HOW IT WORKS

  • Choose a destination: Moon (7 stories), Mars (17) or Deep Space (12).
  • Open a machine's page and read its story in four short chapters: why it was built, its hardest moment, what it discovered, and its legacy.
  • Press "Listen to my story" to hear it narrated (AI-generated voice).
  • Check the status badge (still active or gone silent), the mission stats, a Did You Know fact and NASA photos.
  • Finish with a quick quiz that explains every answer.

The home page has an interactive 3D solar system, and the Mars Odyssey page embeds NASA's Eyes on the Solar System.

HOW WE DEVELOPED IT

We wrote the stories from NASA sources in simple English for high school students, and built one shared page template so every machine has the same easy-to-follow structure. The site is a fast static web app that installs like an app . Mission facts and images come from NASA.gov, NASA Science, the NASA Mars Exploration Program, the NASA Image and Video Library and NASA's Eyes on the Solar System, plus Wikimedia Commons for historical photographs.

HOPE TO ACHIEVE

We want students to feel something about a spacecraft, not only memorise it. If a student remembers Surveyor 1 as well as Apollo, the project has worked.

HIGHLIGHTED FEATURES

  • 36 first-person stories across the Moon, Mars and deep space
  • "Listen to my story" audio narration on every page
  • Status badge: still active or gone silent
  • Quick quiz with explanations
  • Interactive 3D solar system
  • Free, no account.

BENEFITS

  • Makes space history easier to understand and remember for high school students
  • Gives lesser-known missions the attention that Apollo usually gets
  • Audio and text together help more learners

TOOLS AND TECHNOLOGIES

React 19, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Three.js, Motion, PWA service worker, Vercel hosting.

LINKS

  • GitHub: https://github.com/thzihanofficial/ssg-or-hof
  • 240-second video: https://youtu.be/-ysY9GMZtXE

USE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE

  • Google AI Studio: helped build the web app (code).
  • Claude: rewrote and fact-checked the story text.
  • ElevenLabs: AI-generated narration voices (audio on the site and in the videos).
  • Gemini and Google Flow: AI-generated images and video clips in the project videos.

The audio on the site is labelled "AI-generated voice".
